subject: CareBridge POC — LLM data safeguards, IP & subprocessor questions
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@carebridgeanalytics.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Aug 2025 13:24:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify training / IP / subprocessors for POC

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile looked promising for our clinical summarization use case. Before we move the POC forward we need a few clarifications from an IP & privacy standpoint so Legal can sign off: 

1) No-model-learning commitment: we need written confirmation that CareBridge customer data used in the POC will not be used to train or adapt models (no fine-tuning, no retention for model improvement). Please indicate any exceptions (telemetry required for safety? aggregate telemetry?)

2) Prompt/response ownership: our clinical notes and outputs contain PHI. We need clarity that CareBridge retains ownership/licensing of both prompts (input) and generated outputs, and that Redwood will not claim derivative rights to outputs.

3) Subprocessors & cross-border transfers: can you provide the current subprocessor list, and confirm whether any subprocessors will process data outside the US during the POC? Also need to know if you support onshore KMS (US-only) for key management.

If you can put these in a short email or send the DPA we can loop in our procurement. We aim to finish legal review this week.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Lin
Head of Data Platform
CareBridge Analytics

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@carebridgeanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Aug 2025 16:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarify training / IP / subprocessors for POC

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Attaching our standard DPA draft + current subprocessor inventory for the POC. High level answers below, and I've looped in Marissa (AE) and Logan (privacy/ops) to confirm ops details and next steps.

1) No-model-learning: Redwood will agree to a scoped no-training commitment for the CareBridge POC. Operationally we implement this via: (a) an opt-out tag on the tenant so requests are not persisted to training datasets; (b) a KV/prefix cache that expires on request lifecycle termination. Exceptions: minimal aggregated telemetry (error rates, token counts) are retained for service health. We can add explicit language to the DPA to exclude telemetry aggregated for health/metrics and to prohibit use for model improvement.

2) Prompt/response IP: We will commit that CareBridge retains rights to inputs and outputs produced by the POC; Redwood will not assert derivative ownership or rights to the generated outputs. We can add a short clause to the DPA and an operational statement about exportability of outputs on request.

3) Subprocessors & KMS: Current subprocessor list attached. For the POC we will not route data outside the US by default. We support US-only KMS (onshore) for encryption keys for customers on an enterprise plan; for the POC we can enable a US KMS-backed tenant.

Next steps: I'm attaching: redwood-dpa-draft-20250811.pdf and subprocessors-20250811.csv. If Legal has redlines, we can: 1) accept limited redlines in DocuSign, or 2) set up a 30-min call with Ben from Legal to walk through. Which do you prefer?

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-dpa-draft-20250811.pdf (DPA v0.9), subprocessors-20250811.csv (current list)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@carebridgeanalytics.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2025 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Clarify training / IP / subprocessors for POC

Sarah — quick note from Legal on the proposed DPA redlines. I've attached a short redline doc (suggested-dpa-redlines-vanessa-20250812.docx). Key points: 

- No-training: We can accept a tenant-level no-training covenant for the POC. Proposed language: "Provider shall not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any machine learning models used to provide the Services, except for aggregated anonymized telemetry for service health that cannot be re-identified."

- Prompt/response ownership: Add explicit sentence: "Customer retains all rights to Customer Data and to outputs generated by the Services from Customer Data; Provider shall have no ownership or derivative rights in such outputs."

- Proof/evidence: Customer asked for evidence flow — for the POC we can provide: subprocessor inventory, audit logs for request handling (30-day window), and an ops runbook describing tenant opt-out enforcement. For formal requests we can generate a short evidence pack (CSV + minimal logs).

- KMS/onshore keys: We can enable customer-managed keys (CMKs) in a US-only HSM/KMS for the POC. There is operational lead time (~3 business days) to enable and rotate keys, which Marissa can coordinate.

If this sounds OK we can accept these clauses and prepare a DocuSign-ready DPA for signature. If CareBridge requires longer-term contractual guarantees (longer retention of proof, SOC2 addenda, or on-prem deployment) we can discuss under an enterprise agreement.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
attachments: suggested-dpa-redlines-vanessa-20250812.docx

From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@carebridgeanalytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@carebridgeanalytics.com
Date: Wed, 13 Aug 2025 11:07:00 -0400
Subject: Re: CareBridge POC — LLM data safeguards, IP & subprocessor questions

Ben / Vanessa — this is helpful, thanks. Two follow-ups before we sign: 

A) Evidence retention window: you mentioned 30-day request logs — can that be extended to 90 days for the POC? Our audit team likes a slightly longer window to validate no-training assertions.

B) Exportability: we need an automated way to export generated outputs and a manifest of prompts used during the POC. Ideally a per-tenant S3 export (SFTP acceptable) that we can retrieve on-demand. Will that be available in the POC workspace (not just an ops ticket)?

C) KMS proof: we need confirmation that patient-level PHI will be encrypted with customer-provided KMS keys and that Redwood personnel cannot decrypt without our consent. A short statement describing KMS key access controls would be great.

If you can confirm A/B/C we can get procurement moving and sign the DPA.

Best,
Sarah

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@carebridgeanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Aug 2025 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: CareBridge POC — LLM data safeguards, IP & subprocessor questions

Sarah — thanks, quick answers below and next steps: 

A) Evidence retention: we can extend the request/audit log retention for the CareBridge POC to 90 days. That will be documented in the DPA Appendix A (evidence & logs).

B) Exportability: we'll enable a tenant-level export function for the POC: per-tenant S3 export (or SFTP) with a manifest that includes: request id, timestamp, prompt hash (or prompt snippet if you prefer), and the generated output. The export will be accessible via the POC workspace UI and as an ops API endpoint so you won't need a manual ticket.

C) KMS proof: we will enable a customer-managed KMS key stored in a US-only HSM. Redwood's production personnel will not have the decryption key; we will document the key-access model in the runbook and include an access-control statement in the DPA: "Customer managed keys; Provider does not have administrative access to customer key material and cannot decrypt customer data without explicit customer authorization."

Next steps: Ben will fold the language into the DPA and I'll prepare the DocuSign envelope. If you want a short (20–30 min) technical walk-through with Logan to demo the export and KMS flows, we can do that tomorrow morning. I've included HubSpot + DocuSign links above; I'll send the DocuSign when Ben confirms redlines.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to getting the POC signed.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
